headline: Meta has released its Muse AI assistant as an iPad app, about a month after the phone version, with more connections to business tools and shops.
score_reason: Pool 5 lowered by 1: the iPad release was on 7 Oct, before the window, and is an incremental platform extension.
importance_line: Muse users can now run Meta's AI agent on a tablet and let it act in more work and shopping services, though the 6.6 million install figure is an outside estimate and agents can still be blocked by websites.
summary: TechCrunch reports that Meta announced on Wednesday 7 Oct 2026 that its Muse AI assistant, which can book tables, order groceries and make purchases through accounts users choose to connect, is now an iPad app, and that Sensor Tower estimates Muse has passed 6.6 million installs since its 8 Sep launch. The iPad release adds connectors for business tools such as Asana, Canva and QuickBooks, and Meta says it is working with partners on an open standard so that AI agents can identify themselves to websites that might otherwise block them as bots.
notes: Pool link was Dataconomy, a copy of TechCrunch's text; credited to TechCrunch and linked to it. Score 5 to 4 (7 Oct event).
